1.0 Scope Of Work

This method statement covers the safe drilling operations from spud to total depth, including:

☐ Rig up and BOP installation ☐ Drilling surface hole (_____________")

☐ Running and cementing conductor casing ☐ Drilling intermediate hole (_____________")

☐ Running and cementing surface casing ☐ Drilling production hole (_____________")

☐ BOP testing and function checks ☐ Logging and evaluation

☐ Directional drilling (if applicable) ☐ Running and cementing production casing

☐ Well control drills ☐ Preparing to hand over for completion

All operations shall be conducted in accordance with the approved drilling program, API standards, and

relevant statutory requirements.

5.0 Pre-Spud Procedure

5.1 Rig Acceptance and Site Preparation:

• Verify rig is positioned correctly over well center

• Check rig level and alignment

• Conduct rig acceptance inspection

• Verify all safety systems operational

• Check BOP and accumulator function

• Test all alarms and communications

5.2 Pre-Spud Meeting and Drills:

• Conduct pre-spud safety meeting with all personnel

• Review drilling program and critical depths

• Conduct well control drill (all crews)

• Conduct H2S drill (if applicable)

• Conduct fire and emergency drills

• Review stuck pipe prevention measures

5.3 Conductor Installation (if not pre-installed):

• Drill conductor hole (_____________" x _____________ ft)

• Run conductor casing (_____________" x _____________ ft)

• Cement conductor with _____________ sxs

• Weld conductor to wellhead

6.0 Drilling Procedure By Hole Section

6.1 Surface Hole Drilling (_____________" to _____________ ft):

• Make up BHA: Bit + mud motor + MWD + drill collars + HWDP + drill pipe

• Spud in and drill with _____________ GPM, _____________ RPM

• Maintain mud properties per program (MW _____________ ppg, PV _____________ cp)

• Monitor drilling parameters (WOB, ROP, torque, pressure)

• Perform flow checks at connections

• Collect cuttings samples every _____________ ft

• At section TD, circulate bottoms up and condition mud

• Run wireline logs as required

6.2 Surface Casing Running and Cementing:

• Inspect casing and drift all joints

• Make up casing with _____________ connections

• Fill casing every _____________ joints while running

• Land casing at _____________ ft with _____________ ft above seabed

• Circulate and condition mud before cementing

• Pump cement slurry (lead _____________ sxs, tail _____________ sxs)

• Displace with _____________ bbls at _____________ bpm

• Bump plug with _____________ psi

• Wait on cement (WOC) _____________ hours

• Nipple up BOP and test to _____________ psi

6.3 Intermediate Hole Drilling (_____________" to _____________ ft):

• Drill out cement and shoe track

• Perform formation integrity test (FIT) at _____________ psi

• Drill ahead with _____________ GPM, _____________ RPM

• Monitor for kicks and losses continuously

• Perform directional work as per program

• Circulate and condition mud at connections

• At section TD, circulate and condition for logs

• Run wireline logs

6.4 Intermediate Casing Running and Cementing:

• Similar procedure as surface casing

• Ensure centralizers at _____________ ft spacing

• Cement with _____________ sxs lead, _____________ sxs tail

• WOC _____________ hours

• Test BOP to _____________ psi

6.5 Production Hole Drilling (_____________" to TD @ _____________ ft):

• Drill out shoe and perform FIT

• Drill to TD with optimized parameters

• Monitor for H2S if expected

• Perform wiper trips as needed

• At TD, circulate bottoms up and condition mud

• Run comprehensive log suite

6.6 Production Casing Running and Cementing:

• Run casing with _____________ centralizers

• Fill casing every _____________ joints

• Land at _____________ ft

• Cement with _____________ sxs lead, _____________ sxs tail

• Displace with _____________ bbls

• Bump plug and hold pressure

• WOC _____________ hours

• Test casing to _____________ psi

7.0 Well Control Procedures

7.1 Primary Well Control (Mud):

• Maintain mud weight between _____________ and _____________ ppg

• Monitor pit volume continuously (_____________ bbl increase alarm)

• Monitor flow show at connections

• Check mud properties every _____________ hours

• Keep mud logging unit operational

7.2 Secondary Well Control (BOP):

• BOP tested to _____________ psi every _____________ days

• Function test BOP every _____________ days

• Accumulator pressure maintained at _____________ psi

• Choke manifold tested weekly

• All crew members trained in BOP operations

7.3 Kick Detection and Handling:

• Flow check immediately if pit gain or flow observed

• If positive flow, shut well in using hard shut-in procedure

• Record SIDPP and SICP

• Use driller's method or wait and weight method per program

• Circulate kick out through choke manifold

• Maintain _____________ psi on casing at all times

• Monitor for gas at surface

7.4 Well Control Drills:

• Conduct weekly well control drills (all crews)

• Record drill times and performance

• Debrief after each drill

• Maintain well control training for all personnel

8.0 Directional Drilling Procedure (If Applicable)

8.1 Well Trajectory:

• Target coordinates: _____________ N/S, _____________ E/W, _____________ ft TVD

• Kick-off point: _____________ ft

• Build rate: _____________°/100 ft to _____________° inclination

• Hold angle: _____________° to _____________ ft

• Drop rate: _____________°/100 ft

8.2 Survey Program:

• Survey interval: every _____________ ft drilled

• Survey type: ☐ MWD ☐ Gyro ☐ Magnetic single shot

• Calculate and plot actual vs planned trajectory

• Correct trajectory if deviation > _____________ ft

8.3 Anti-Collision:

• Conduct anti-collision analysis before drilling

• Maintain minimum separation factor > 1.5

• Plot proximity to offset wells

• Stop drilling if separation factor < 1.0

9.0 Daily Operations And Reporting

9.1 Daily Drilling Report (IADC format):

• Report prepared by: Toolpusher/Company Man

• Submitted by: _____________ hrs daily

• Contents:

- Operations summary for last 24 hours

- Current depth and status

- Drilling parameters (WOB, RPM, GPM, SPP, ROP)

- Mud properties and pit volumes

- BOP status and test results

- Personnel on board

- HSE incidents and near misses

- Planned operations for next 24 hours

9.2 End of Well Report:

• Final well schematic with depths and casing sizes

• Final drilling parameters summary

• Bit records and dull grading

• Mud recap and chemical usage

• Time breakdown by operation

• Lessons learned and recommendations

10.0 H2S Safety Procedures

10.1 H2S Monitoring:

• Fixed H2S sensors at: rig floor, shale shakers, mud pits, BOP area

• Personal H2S monitors for all personnel

• H2S monitors bump tested before each tour

• Wind direction indicator (windsock) visible from all areas

• Alarm set points: 10 ppm (caution), 15 ppm (warning), 20+ ppm (evacuate)

10.2 H2S Contingency Plan:

• Upon H2S alarm (10+ ppm):

1. All personnel don escape packs immediately

2. Move upwind to muster point

3. Account for all personnel

4. H2S team dons SCBA and investigates source

5. If increasing, evacuate non-essential personnel

• Escape packs located at: rig floor, catwalk, shale shakers, living quarters

• SCBA units at: rig floor, BOP area, safe zone

• Weekly H2S drills conducted

11.0 Environmental Protection Measures

11.1 Waste Management:

• Cuttings disposal: ☐ Offshore discharge ☐ Cuttings reinjection ☐ Skip and ship

• Mud and chemical spills: Spill kits at all handling areas

• Used oil: Collected in labeled drums for recycling

• Domestic waste: Segregated and disposed ashore

11.2 Discharge Permits:

• All discharges comply with local regulations

• No discharge of oil or oily water

• Maintain discharge log

12.0 Emergency Response Procedures

12.1 Emergency Contacts:

• Rig Medic: ______________ Channel: ____ Phone: ______________

• Onshore Base: ______________ Phone: ______________

• Coast Guard (offshore): Channel 16 / ______________

• Hospital: ______________ Phone: ______________

• Operator Emergency: ______________ Phone: ______________

12.2 Emergency Scenarios:

• WELL CONTROL EMERGENCY:

- Shut in well immediately

- Sound general alarm

- Muster at designated safe area

- Activate emergency response plan

- Notify operator and authorities

• H2S RELEASE:

- Don escape packs/SCBA

- Move upwind

- Account for personnel

- Investigate source with H2S team

• MEDICAL EMERGENCY:

- Call medic to location

- Administer first aid

- Prepare for evacuation if required

- Contact onshore base

• FIRE:

- Sound alarm

- Attempt to extinguish if safe

- Evacuate if fire grows

- Muster and account for all

12.3 Muster Points and Escape Routes:

• Primary Muster: ______________

• Secondary Muster: ______________

• Abandon Rig Muster (offshore): ______________

• Escape routes posted at all exits
